default.notes: All visitors need a visa arranged through a state-approved tour operator as part of an organised tour; tourism has been essentially closed since 2020 and applications are accepted only when tours are running.

US.notes: The ban is imposed by the US side: US passports are invalid for travel to, in or through North Korea under US law unless specially validated by the State Department.

KR.notes: South Korean citizens cannot enter North Korea — inter-Korean travel requires special authorisation from both governments and is not available to tourists.

RU.notes: Limited Russian group tours resumed in 2024 — the visa is arranged by the tour operator through the DPRK embassy as part of the package.

MY.notes: A visa via a state-approved tour would be required, but Malaysia itself has barred its citizens from travelling to North Korea since 2017.

KP.notes: Home country — although exit and re-entry are tightly controlled by the state for DPRK citizens.
